evidence.quote: {{root|en|ine-pro|*bʰerHǵ-}} The {{glossary|adjective}} is from {{inh|en|enm|bright}}, from {{inh|en|ang|berht}}, {{m|ang|beorht}}, {{m|ang|bryht}}, {{m|ang|byrht}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*berht}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*berhtaz|t=bright}}, ultimately from {{der|en|ine-pro|*bʰerHǵ-|t=to gleam, shine, whiten}}. The {{glossary|noun}} is derived from {{inh|en|enm|bright|t=brightness, brilliance; daylight; light}}, from {{m|enm|bright|pos=adjective}}:<ref>{{R:MED Online|pos=n|id=MED6030}}</ref> see above. {{col-top|2|cog}} Cognate with {{cog|sco|bricht|t=bright}}, {{cog|da|bjært|t=bright}}, {{cog|fo,is|bjartur|t=bright}}, {{cog|nn|bjart|t=bright}}, {{cog|sv|bjärt|t=bright}}, {{cog|got|𐌱𐌰𐌹𐍂𐌷𐍄𐍃|t=

"radiating or reflecting light," Old English bryht, metathesis of beorht "bright;… See origin and meaning of bright. from Proto-Germanic *berhtaz "bright" (source also of Old Saxon berht , Old Norse bjartr , Old High German beraht , Gothic bairhts "bright"), from PIE root *bhereg- "to shine; bright, white.

proposed_usageNote: This surface form has other senses (3 English etymology sections, colour, light / shine). The usage curve may mix them.
